Build a mesh that describes itself

Source: R/mesh_space.R
brain_mesh.Rd

Assembles vertices, faces and a mesh_space() into one object, checking they agree. Reading a surface file and assembling the pieces by hand is done in several places across the ecosystem, and each one decided independently whether faces were counted from 0 or from 1 – which is why ggseg.formats inflated surfaces are 0-based, ggseg.meshes cortical surfaces are 1-based, and consumers carry code to cope. Declaring the base and having it checked makes that disagreement impossible to introduce again.

Usage

brain_mesh(vertices, faces, space, face_index_base)

Arguments

vertices

A data.frame of x, y, z.

faces

A data.frame of i, j, k.

space

A mesh_space() describing what the coordinates mean.

face_index_base

0L or 1L – the number the file's face indices count from. Required.

Value

A list of vertices and faces, carrying mesh_space and face_index_base attributes.

Details

face_index_base has no default on purpose. A default would be a fourth independent decision, and the point is that the caller states what their file actually contains.

The faces are checked against the base rather than taken on trust: the smallest index must equal the base and the largest must be the last vertex counted from it. A mesh that declares 0 while holding 1-based indices renders with one vertex silently misplaced and the last face out of range, which is the failure this refuses.

See also

Other mesh spaces: mesh_space(), set_mesh_space()

Examples

brain_mesh(
  vertices = data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1), z = c(0, 0, 0)),
  faces = data.frame(i = 0L, j = 1L, k = 2L),
  space = mesh_space("fsaverage5", "left", anatomical = FALSE),
  face_index_base = 0L
)
#> $vertices
#>   x y z
#> 1 0 0 0
#> 2 1 0 0
#> 3 0 1 0
#> 
#> $faces
#>   i j k
#> 1 0 1 2
#> 
#> attr(,"face_index_base")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"mesh_space")
#> <mesh_space> (v1)
#> • vertex space: "fsaverage5"
#> • hemisphere: "left"
#> • not anatomical, no MNI305 mapping
#> • units: "mm"
